findings.old_behavior: When metadata buffer size overflow (integer wraparound) is detected, an error message 'Metadata buffer size overflow.' is logged without any diagnostic details.
findings.new_behavior: When metadata buffer size overflow is detected, the error message includes the actual size values (size, size2) and the device name, formatted as 'Metadata buffer size overflow %zu + %zu on %s.'.
findings.compatibility_reason: The error message format for metadata buffer overflow has changed. Any tool, script, monitoring system, or test that parses lvm stderr/log output and matches against the exact error string 'Metadata buffer size overflow.' will fail to match the new message. The message now includes size values and device name which changes both the text and number of tokens.
findings.why_not_internal_only: The metadata buffer size overflow error path is reachable via the config_file_read_fd function which is called during lvm metadata parsing on config/metadata reads. Error messages from lvm commands (pvscan, vgscan, lvmconf, etc.) are visible to users in stderr and potentially in system logs. The user_visible_output surface is marked semi_stable.
findings.uncertainty: Low. The error message text change is directly visible in the diff. The only uncertainty is whether any external tooling depends on parsing this specific error message string.
findings.recommended_review: No manual review needed. The error message change is straightforward. If there are lvm wrapper scripts or monitoring tools that parse stderr for this specific message text, they would need updating.
findings.test_recommendation: Verify that the new error message format includes the correct size and device name. Compile the patched binary and trigger the metadata buffer overflow condition (by passing a crafted metadata size that causes integer wraparound) to confirm the new message format.
